---
title: "Clustering"
---

This section examines whether the playlist contains meaningful internal structure when no explicit labels such as genre or artist are used.

Clustering allows us to move beyond subjective listening and analyse how tracks group together purely based on their audio features.

The analysis combines hierarchical clustering, a feature heatmap, and dimensionality reduction through PCA.

## Dendrogram

![Hierarchical Clustering Dendrogram](dendrogram_clean.png)

The dendrogram shows how tracks group together based on similarity across all selected audio features.

## Interpretation

At higher levels of the tree, a small number of broader clusters emerge. However, the structure is not sharply divided. Many tracks merge gradually, indicating that differences between groups are subtle rather than clearly separated.

This suggests that the playlist does not consist of distinct categories, but rather a continuum of musical characteristics.

## Feature Heatmap

![Feature Heatmap (per track)](track_heatmap_clean.png)

The heatmap provides a detailed view of how individual tracks behave across features such as energy, loudness, danceability, acousticness, instrumentalness, and tempo.

## Interpretation

Clear horizontal patterns appear, where groups of tracks share similar feature profiles. Some tracks are consistently high in energy and loudness, reflecting more production-heavy material. Others show higher acousticness or lower instrumentalness.

Energy, loudness, acousticness, and instrumentalness show the strongest variation across tracks, while tempo remains relatively stable.

This indicates that clustering is driven more by production intensity and texture than by tempo.

## K-means Clustering

![K-means Clusters (k = 3)](kmeans_clusters.png)

K-means clustering groups the tracks into three clusters and projects them into two dimensions using PCA.

## Interpretation

The clusters are visible, but not cleanly separated. There is overlap between groups, with tracks positioned between cluster centres.

This indicates that the playlist forms a continuous feature space rather than clearly distinct categories.

## PCA Representation

![PCA of Audio Features](pca_plot.png)

The PCA plot shows the distribution of tracks across the two most important dimensions of variation.

## Interpretation

The first component (PC1) reflects production intensity, while the second component (PC2) represents variation in emotional tone and vocal presence.

Tracks spread along these axes, but remain concentrated within a limited region, indicating variation within a constrained feature space.

## Key Findings

Clustering reveals that the playlist is structured, but not in a strictly categorical way.

The dendrogram shows hierarchical grouping, while the heatmap highlights consistent feature patterns across tracks. K-means clustering and PCA demonstrate that these groupings overlap rather than forming clearly separated clusters.

The most important distinctions between tracks are driven by production intensity and sonic texture, particularly reflected in energy, loudness, acousticness, and instrumentalness.

## Connection to the Research Question

Although the playlist appears diverse in terms of genre, language, and artist, the clustering analysis shows that this diversity is organised within a consistent feature space.

Tracks do not group according to external labels, but according to shared structural characteristics. This indicates that underlying audio features play a stronger role in defining similarity than stylistic categories.

As a result, the playlist exhibits underlying structural consistency, despite its apparent diversity.
